claims.feature: other: time compression in one sentence
claims.claim: Hobb advises skipping a dull stretch of travel by summarising it in one sentence, and supplies the sample sentence herself.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'What Works For Me', robinhobb.com blog, 2022
claims.quote: After four days of punishing travel, they reached a small holding
claims.page: Section: I don't want to write the next scene

claims.claim: Hobb says a chapter may consist of a single sentence.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'What Works For Me', robinhobb.com blog, 2022
claims.quote: You can have a one sentence chapter if you want
claims.page: Section: I don't want to write the next scene

claims.claim: Hobb rejects the word processor's thesaurus because it offers the same synonyms every other writer is using, and recommends a paper Roget's instead.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'What Works For Me', robinhobb.com blog, 2022
claims.quote: the same synonyms that every other writer is using

claims.claim: Hobb gives as a revision-pass example replacing a red car with candy apple red with metal flake.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'What Works For Me', robinhobb.com blog, 2022
claims.quote: The car isn't red, it's candy apple red with metal flake

claims.claim: Groell, the Random House editor of Hobb, Martin and others, says her first read of a book is close line-reading and individual sentence editing.
claims.source: Anne Groell, executive SFF editor, Random House USA, interviewed by Julie Crisp, 2016
claims.quote: I do the really close line-reading and individual sentence editing

claims.claim: Groell says she averages about 25 pages an hour, or 200 pages a day, on that first close read.
claims.source: Anne Groell, executive SFF editor, Random House USA, interviewed by Julie Crisp, 2016
claims.quote: I average about 25 pages an hour, or 200 pages a day

claims.claim: The Idle Woman says Bingtown could belong to an entirely different age than the Six Duchies.
claims.source: The Idle Woman (pseudonymous reviewer), 'Ship of Magic (1998): Robin Hobb', 2013
claims.quote: Bingtown could belong to an entirely different age than the Six Duchies

claims.claim: The Idle Woman says trade, shipping and merchants' colonies give Bingtown a distinctly seventeenth-century feel in contrast with the medievalism of the Farseer trilogy.
claims.source: The Idle Woman (pseudonymous reviewer), 'Ship of Magic (1998): Robin Hobb', 2013

claims.claim: Goldstein criticises Hobb's habit of repeating things, as if she did not trust readers to remember them from one chapter to the next.
claims.source: Lisa Goldstein, novelist, reviewing Dragon Haven in Strange Horizons, 2010
claims.quote: trust her readers to remember them from one chapter to the next

claims.claim: Goldstein says the writing seemed tired and repetitious in Dragon Keeper and is tightened in Dragon Haven.
claims.source: Lisa Goldstein, novelist, reviewing Dragon Haven in Strange Horizons, 2010
claims.quote: which seemed tired and repetitious in the earlier book

claims.claim: Goldstein complains that very little in Dragon Haven could not have been guessed by an astute reader.
claims.source: Lisa Goldstein, novelist, reviewing Dragon Haven in Strange Horizons, 2010
claims.quote: Very little happens that couldn't have been guessed by an astute reader

claims.claim: Hobb says fan fiction closes up the space she has engineered into the story.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'The Fan Fiction Rant', robinhobb.com (page since removed)
claims.quote: closes up the space that I have engineered into the story

claims.claim: Hobb objects that the reader is then told what he must think rather than being allowed to observe the characters and draw his own conclusions.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'The Fan Fiction Rant', robinhobb.com (page since removed)
claims.quote: told what he must think rather than being allowed to observe

claims.claim: Hobb says that if something is left nebulous in her text it is because she intends it to be nebulous.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'The Fan Fiction Rant', robinhobb.com (page since removed)
claims.quote: If something is left nebulous, it is because the author intends

claims.claim: Hobb says a writer puts a great deal of thought into what goes into the story and what does not.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'The Fan Fiction Rant', robinhobb.com (page since removed)
claims.quote: A writer puts a great deal of thought into what goes
